notes.1: The majority of candidates knew the definition of the term community.
notes.2: Many candidates found it difficult to process the information in order to answer the question. Only a minority were able to work out that the first species should be U. �PAGE�10
notes.3: This was well answered by the more able candidates and almost half of the less able candidates were also able to process the information.
notes.4: The majority of candidates answered this correctly.
notes.5: The majority of less able candidates did not realise that the endoplasmic reticulum or lysosomes have only a single membrane.
notes.6: The majority of candidates answered this correctly. However, a significant number of less able candidates thought that starch grains were not visible in a suitably stained plant cell. Those candidates who had carried out practical microscopy were more likely to answer correctly.
notes.7: It was encouraging that almost all of the more able candidates and almost a half of the less able candidates realised that ribosomes were so small that they would not be seen using a microscope with a resolution of 200nm.
notes.8: It was encouraging that over half of the candidates could identify the nucleolus and calculate its size.
notes.9: Less able candidates continue to have difficulty in understanding the roles of the components of the cell surface membrane.
notes.10: Many candidates realised that depending on concentrations and the presence of membrane proteins, all four processes can allow transport into or out of the cell.
notes.11: More than half of the candidates realised that only the uptake of 6-carbon sugars was stopped by the absence of oxygen, which meant that they were taken up by active transport.
notes.12: The majority of less able candidates thought that sucrose is a reducing sugar. Candidates who have carried out tests on biological molecules should know this is incorrect.
notes.13: Whilst almost all candidates knew that iodine in potassium iodide solution turns black in the presence of starch, many were unable to link the biuret test for protein to the presence of the enzyme amylase.
notes.14: Many of the less able candidates incorrectly thought both amylopectin and cellulose are polymers of α-glucose and almost half thought that adjacent glucose molecules are rotated by 180° in both amylopectin and cellulose. �PAGE�11
notes.15: Almost all of the more able candidates and a significant minority of less able candidates knew amylopectin is a carbohydrate and therefore does not contain nitrogen.
notes.16: Candidates who carefully read the question were able to eliminate any answer containing glycerol, which clearly does not contain C=O bonds. Therefore the only possible answer was A. The basic structural formula of glucose does contain a C=O bond.
notes.17: Many of the less able candidates knew the role of the tertiary protein structure in maintaining the globular shape of enzymes.
notes.18: Those candidates who had carried out the suggested practical work in the syllabus to investigate and explain the effects of temperature, pH, enzyme concentration and substrate were able to answer correctly.
notes.19: This was correctly answered by the more able candidates, whilst more than half of the less able candidates incorrectly selected the activation energy in the absence of the enzyme.
notes.20: Over half the candidates incorrectly thought that a reduction division reduces the chance of mutation.
notes.21: This was well answered by most candidates.
notes.22: The relationship between the number of molecules of DNA and number of chromatids during prophase was not understood by the majority of less able candidates.
notes.23: This was correctly answered by the majority of more able candidates. Candidates who read the question carefully realised that there would be 60 nucleotides to code for the polypeptide.
notes.24: Only a minority of less able candidates were able to identify the correct statement.
notes.25: It was encouraging that most candidates were able to answer this correctly. However, less able candidates found this concept difficult.
notes.26: Many less able candidates do not fully understand the concept of transpiration, and many incorrectly thought that water evaporates from the stomata.
notes.27: Less able candidates continue to find it difficult to understand the process of transpiration and its effects. �PAGE�12
notes.28: This was well answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.29: Whilst the majority of candidates realised that the water potential would be decreased, there were some who incorrectly thought that this was due to diffusion of sucrose into sieve tube elements.
notes.30: Whilst the majority of more able candidates identified the correct answer, many less able candidates were unable to use the information in the diagram to answer the question.
notes.31: Only a minority of candidates correctly realised that only eating shellfish which have fed on raw sewage would increase the risk of contracting cholera.
notes.32: Most of the less able and many of the more able candidates found this question about the immune response challenging.
notes.33: This was well answered by over almost all of the more able candidates.
notes.34: Many less able candidates do not understand the action of antibodies.
notes.35: It was pleasing that the majority of candidates were able to process the information correctly to identify the correct part of the heart.
notes.36: Those candidates who carefully studied the information provided and linked this to their knowledge of the blood vessels were able to select D as the correct answer.
notes.37: Whilst the majority of candidates knew that haemoglobin has the highest affinity for carbon monoxide, fewer than half knew that it had the least affinity for carbon dioxide.
notes.38: The biochemistry of the Bohr effect is poorly understood by less able candidates.
notes.39: This was well answered by almost all the more able candidates. However, a significant number of less able candidates did not realise that exocytotic vesicles would be visible in goblet cells.
notes.40: The majority of less able candidates did not understand that a partial blockage of an artery can only cause cardiovascular disease. �PAGE�13
notes.general_comments:
There was a very good spread of scores. Four questions were answered correctly by 75% or more of
candidates – Questions 1, 4, 21 and 28. Questions 2, 16, 20, 22, 23, 31, 32 and 36 proved to be more
difficult, with fewer than half of the candidates answering them correctly.
